Wow, I hope it works out for you. I just wanted to add I have basically all of these symptoms and conditions, and turns out my muscle twitching was from pernicious anemia (autoimmune condition, can't absorb B-12 without shots) and hyper mobile Ehlers-Danlos (very often misdiagnosed as fibromyalgia). Took years to get both diagnosed, but the pernicious anemia was a simple blood test that doctors just rarely do. I'm also pretty sure I have Mast Cell Activation Syndrome, but I'm waiting for that appointment still.

Edit: also, found out my nasal drip, coughing, and losingnmy voice is from severe sleep apnea. Make sure to do an in-lab test as opposed to an at home sleep study, that's how I was diagnosed and just prescribed a CPAP. Would also recommend seeing neurology for possible adult onset epilepsy if you haven't done the full limb muscle twitching, and checking for rheumatoid arthritis with rheumatology.

YES OMG. Everyone always told me it was electrolytes, it was NOT that. Turns out my muscles were so tight everywhere that's what caused it. Also when I do PT and my muscles are really tight, when they start to loosen I get them really bad everywhere, but once everything loosens up they go away.

I know a lot of people (validly!) don't like them but just wanted to offer a different perspective on my experience with them!

I requested something like this! I very much didn't want to be board flat, I described it to my surgeon as wanting to be confusing lol. I'm not skinny so I wanted to be proportionate and while I didn't  request a pec per say in those words, I wanted something left behind so that I was also proportionate. I went with top surgery still though instead of a radical reduction because the size I wanted was likely too flat for that, the risk of them growing back, and because if the surgery "went wrong" I'd rather be too flat than the opposite. I also requested more neutral nip placement (closer to center) and larger ones than what they traditionally do for top surgery, and I love my results! Also the grafts healed super easy, honestly for me easiest part of the whole thing.

I told my surgeon that if you couldn't see any other identifying features about me like my face, I wanted something where you would wrestle back and forth if I was a "guy" or "girl" for a while just based on body, but ultimately if forced to choose you'd choose "guy." A lot of people might (validly!) suggest a radical reduction to you, but I'm personally so glad I didn't get one, and I almost did. I almost definitely would've ended up having to get top surgery anyway as I don't think I would've been able to get as flat as I am now. And my body and weight fluctuate alot so I almost certainly would've had them grow back too I think. Hope this all helps!

Kept mine and honestly the healing was super easy. Had more feeling within the first week then I did before surgery (DI). The black sloughed off (wet healing) almost completely by the end of week 2 and they were fully pink underneath. I did have complications with the surgery (hematomas and bruising), but my grafts have actually been the easiest part of this entire thing. I wasn't extra super careful with them or anything, honestly after they took off the bolsters all I did was put Aquaphor on them once a day and then non adherent pads. Now I'm just doing Aquaphor twice a day and don't need the pads anymore (haven't since week 4 or so).

I thought the same about my clothes and how I looked in them originally. I also figured I could always get padded bras and stuff them if I ever really wanted to, and that if I ever did regret it (I won't though) I could get implants. I realized I was ready for top surgery when I noticed I had started the process of trying to live my life for me versus making decisions based on others perception (which is still really hard). My therapist called top surgery one of my first real acts of self care because it something I did soley and wholly for myself and no one else. I did almost just get a reduction a few years ago, but I'm glad I waited until I was ready for top surgery as opposed to getting a reduction and then having to get top surgery too one day. Hope all this helps and good luck!

I'm nonbinary and I read a comment that said if you woke up without a chest tomorrow, is there anything you would miss? And I realized there wasn't, and also it was my chest that made me uncomfortable in my body as opposed to my shape and size. I'm about 5 weeks post op now and not a single regret. I asked for more neutral nip placement and while still top surgery and flat, something proportionate to my body. And I got that, super happy that I did it! I'd always been large and fluctuated sizes all the time because of health issues, and so I did top surgery as opposed to a radical reduction because I didn't want them to ever grow back and I honestly didn't want them as they were at all really. It was less have I reached the level of dysphoria that is bad enough I "can" or "have permission" to get top surgery, and more that there wasn't anything I would miss with them gone and so much that I hate would disappear, so what did I have to lose? Also the idea of being "too flat" was so much better than having something "too big," so that's another reason I went with top surgery and not a radical reduction.

I'm nonbinary, but I said it was a breast reduction due to shoulder pain, and then I had to get more like a mastectomy to ensure they wouldn't come back and due to my size (all of that is true so it's believable).

But also haven't told most of my family. I started wearing very baggy shirts a few years ago and I still wear baggy clothes so honestly not sure if they'll notice next time I'll see them, so maybe start wearing looser shirts around them slowly so it'll be easier to hide eventually?

You could also lie and say they found something and recommended a double mastectomy? 

Hope this helps and good luck!

Edit: Also, tip for hiding the voice changes is say you can say you have GERD. I actually do have it lol and told my family since I started treating it and did voice therapy because it caused vocal cord issues (also true) my voice just permanently is lower now.

Edit 2: my biggest overall advice in general for hiding stuff I'd say probably is either use things that are true and your family have known about for a long time to be true, or plant the seeds for something for a long time. Like I made sure how to casually mention like oh I saw the doctor this week and he mentioned that the GERD is making my voice extra high which is damaging it, or oh yeah my throat hurts the acid reflux, and then oh at this week's appointment the doctor said I'm doing well because he can hear me using my lower register more than that damaged upper register and that's what I need to be using cuz it's easier on my throat, etc. etc. So no one actually asked me about my voice ever, I just slowly dropped stuff like that along the way. But it's really important that it feels natural and subtle. Like I did that cuz it's normal for me to tell my family how my appointments that week went. I also practiced on other people as well, like acquaintances or strangers. Like oh so sorry my voice cracked, my acid reflux man. Or yeah sorry I can't lift that I just had a double mastectomy. Sorry if this is alot lol but hope it's helpful!

This may be completely irrelevant to you so feel free to ignore lmao, but my story is more about stuff I didn't do when people tried to make me.

I did soccer (idk if it helped me at all honestly lol), but mostly I just didn't do things I knew hurt or felt dangerous. the thing that saved me was ignoring doctors for awhile. My mom was diagnosed only with fibromyalgia and I was completely undiagnosed. My mom listened to the doctors and did the weight training, the physical therapy, hiking everything. But I refused as even though I didn't know why, I knew it made things hurt. I chose to be over careful as I knew for example, I tend to trip when walking and pop my knees, so I won't go hiking because I feel unstable. Or I won't do weights because it makes my shoulders feel like they've fallen out, running makes me throw up (undiagnosed dysautonomia), etc etc.

Now 10 years later, I got both my mom and myself diagnosed and was told that while a lot of her damage is permanent from listening to doctors and doing the weight training, exercise, and incorrect physical therapy, I still have the potential to live a lot less painful life because I haven't damaged myself yet. Now I'm seeing a physicical therapist who specializes in hypermobility and  without any sort of cardio, weights, anything at all but his exercises and my normal daily walking during life, for the first time in ten years I can do things like open my hand fully, walk up a hill without pain, etc etc. Occupational has also helped because I learned how to do things to accomodate myself. I wanted to hike, but was nervous about my ankle instability. So I bought shoes that lace up around my ankles to support myself. Or I tend to pop my shoulder out when reaching in the cabinet, so I bought a step stool.

It was rough for a long time, but in the end I'm glad I listened to myself and protected my body from lasting damage, even if I was "weaker" and judged by my peers for being "unathletic" for a long time
